case.title: Influenza A with pneumonia
case.summary: Pneumonia caused by influenza A gets one combination code, not separate pneumonia and flu codes.

documents.author: D. Nakamura, MD (Radiology)
documents.text:
EXAM: XR chest, 2 views.
FINDINGS: Patchy bibasilar airspace and interstitial opacities, left greater than right. No effusion or pneumothorax. Cardiomediastinal silhouette within normal limits for technique.
IMPRESSION: Bibasilar opacities, which may reflect multifocal pneumonia, viral or bacterial.

documents.author: K. Abernathy, MD (Emergency Medicine)
documents.text:
CC: fever, cough, body aches.
HPI: 63 y/o F with HTN, HLD, hypothyroidism, obesity presents with 3 days fever to 39.4 at home, dry cough now productive, myalgias, headache, SOB with walking to bathroom. Husband had "the flu" last week. Did not receive flu vaccine this season.
Vitals: T 39.0, HR 108, RR 22, BP 128/74, SpO2 92% RA -> 95% on 2 L NC.
Exam: Ill-appearing, A&Ox3. Coarse crackles bilateral bases. Tachycardic, regular. Abd soft.
Labs: Influenza A/B PCR: Influenza A DETECTED, B not detected. SARS-CoV-2 PCR negative. RSV negative. WBC 6.8 (lymphocytes 9%). Na 129, K 3.8, Cr 0.8, BUN 18, glucose 121. Procalcitonin 0.09. Lactate 1.4.
CXR: bilateral lower lobe patchy opacities.
ED course: oseltamivir 75 mg PO, ceftriaxone 1 g + azithromycin 500 mg IV (empiric CAP coverage), acetaminophen, 1 L NS.
Impression: Influenza A; bilateral pneumonia - viral vs superimposed bacterial. Hyponatremia. Admit.

documents.author: R. Oyelaran, MD (Hospital Medicine)
documents.text:
HISTORY AND PHYSICAL
HPI: 63F, unvaccinated this season, sick contact at home, 3 days of fever, myalgias, cough, exertional dyspnea. Flu A PCR positive. CXR bibasilar opacities. Na 129.
PMH: HTN, HLD, hypothyroidism, obesity (BMI 33.4).
Meds: amlodipine 10 mg, rosuvastatin 10 mg, levothyroxine 100 mcg.
Exam: T 38.6, HR 102, RR 20, SpO2 95% 2 L. Bibasilar crackles. No edema. Euvolemic to slightly dry.
ASSESSMENT/PLAN:
1. Influenza A with bilateral pneumonia - oseltamivir 75 mg BID x 5 days. Continue ceftriaxone/azithro pending procalcitonin trend; low suspicion for bacterial superinfection (PCT 0.09). O2 to keep SpO2 > 92%. Droplet precautions.
2. Hyponatremia - Na 129, likely hypovolemic from poor PO intake/insensible losses. NS 75 mL/h, BMP q12h, avoid overcorrection.
3. HTN - continue amlodipine.
4. HLD - continue rosuvastatin.
5. Hypothyroidism - continue levothyroxine; TSH 2.1 in 07/2026.
6. Obesity, BMI 33.4 - counsel outpatient.
DVT ppx enoxaparin. Full code.

documents.author: A. Benitez, RN
documents.text: Droplet precautions maintained. Pt resting, coughing intermittently, productive of small amt white sputum. SpO2 93-95% on 1 L NC, trialed RA at 01:30 with SpO2 92-93%, left off O2 per order. T 37.6 at midnight, acetaminophen given for myalgias with relief. Taking PO fluids well, ~900 mL this shift. IVF NS @ 75 mL/h infusing. Voiding qs. Ambulated to BR independently, steady. Husband called, updated per pt request.

documents.author: Clinical Laboratory
documents.text:
Sodium trend: 09/20 20:15 129; 09/21 06:00 131; 09/21 18:00 133; 09/22 05:45 135.
Serum osmolality (09/20): 268 mOsm/kg. Urine Na (09/20): < 20 mmol/L. Urine osm 540.
Procalcitonin: 0.09 (09/20) -> 0.07 (09/22).
Blood cultures x2 (09/20): no growth at 48 h. Sputum culture: normal respiratory flora.
WBC 6.8 -> 5.9. Cr 0.8 -> 0.7.

documents.author: R. Oyelaran, MD (Hospital Medicine)
documents.text:
S: Fevers breaking, myalgias better. Cough persists. Ambulating with RN.
O: Tmax 37.8, HR 88, RR 18, SpO2 94% RA (weaned off O2 overnight). Na 129 -> 133 -> 135. Repeat PCT 0.07. Blood cx NGTD.
A/P:
1. Influenza A pneumonia (viral) - PCT low x2, cultures negative; stop ceftriaxone/azithromycin. This is pneumonia due to influenza; no evidence of bacterial pneumonia. Continue oseltamivir, day 3 of 5.
2. Hyponatremia - improved to 135 with IVF; saline lock today.
3. HTN, HLD, hypothyroidism - home meds.
4. Obesity BMI 33.4.

documents.author: R. Oyelaran, MD (Hospital Medicine)
documents.text:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admit 09/20/2026 - Discharge 09/23/2026. Home.
Principal diagnosis: Influenza A with pneumonia.
Secondary diagnoses: Hyponatremia (hypovolemic), resolved. Hypertension. Hyperlipidemia. Hypothyroidism. Obesity, BMI 33.4.
Hospital course: Presented with fever, cough, hypoxemia; influenza A PCR positive with bibasilar opacities. Treated with oseltamivir and initially empiric antibiotics, discontinued HD2 given low procalcitonin x2 and negative cultures; pneumonia felt to be due to influenza. Weaned to room air HD2. Hyponatremia corrected with isotonic fluids (129 -> 135).
Discharge meds: oseltamivir 75 mg BID to complete 5 days; home amlodipine, rosuvastatin, levothyroxine.
Follow-up: PCP 1 week with BMP; flu vaccine when recovered; household members advised re: prophylaxis.

gold.explanation: Pneumonia due to confirmed influenza A takes the single combination code J10.00 (influenza with unspecified type of pneumonia). Bacterial pneumonia was considered and explicitly dropped, so no separate pneumonia code is added. J18.9 and J12.9 carry Excludes1 notes for pneumonia with influenza, and J10.1 is the wrong axis. A naive system codes J18.9 + J10.1, or keys on the ED's 'viral vs superimposed bacterial'. Hyponatremia (E87.1) is the CC, giving DRG 194.

codes.description: Influenza due to other identified influenza virus with unspecified type of pneumonia

baseline.reason: Influenza A is a PCR-confirmed seasonal influenza, so J10.00 (influenza due to other identified influenza virus with unspecified type of pneumonia) was chosen for 'influenza with pneumonia, viral'. A coder may prefer J10.08 or another more specific pneumonia code; this needs review. Hypoxemia (R09.02) was mentioned in the discharge summary but is integral to the pneumonia, so it was not coded. Hypovolemia was documented as the cause of the hyponatremia, so E86.1 was added (E86.1 hypovolemia); this should be verified. Obesity E66.9 was coded with BMI Z68.33. Under FY2025+ guidelines obesity may be reported as E66.811 (class 1) if class is documented, but it is not, so E66.9 stands. Z28.310 (unvaccinated for influenza) is optional.
